newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania privatisation fund sold off 2,500 firms.
newsitem.headline: Romania privatisation fund sold off 2,500 firms.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency said on Tuesday it has privatised 2,500 state companies, or 39.7 percent of the enterprises slated for selloff, in almost four years since the launch of privatisation.

From late 1992 to September 20, the State Ownership Fund (FPS) turned private 79 big companies, 557 medium-sized enterprises and 1,864 small companies, putting some 160 million shares in private hands, a FPS statement said.
Of the total 2,500 companies, 1,017 firms -- most of them in trade, tourism, construction, services, the textile and food industries and transport -- were sold this year, the FPS said.
Privatisation is a plank of market reforms which Romania launched after the 1989 collapse of communism.
When the FPS started privatisations in 1992 it held 70 percent of around 6,000 companies.

In a separate mass selloff launched last October some 15 million adult Romanians were offered around 600 million shares, or stakes of up to 60 percent, in some 4,000 companies in exchange for coupons. Subcription under the mass selloff was put at around 90 percent when it ended in March.
The rest of at least 40 percent was earmarked for cash sales to local and foreign investors, with the FPS in charge of those sales.
Share packages representing 5.0 to 40 percent of 447 companies were auctioned off this year, the statement said.
Critics of Romanian privatisation say the process has been slow and cumbersome.

Privatisation officials blame the delay on scarce domestic capital and thin foreign investor interest. But they say the picture is different now as domestic capital has accumulated and bigger foreign investors show an interest in Romania.

Direct foreign investment since since 1989 stands at around $2.0 billion, compared with some $11 billion in neighbouring Hungary or over $10 billion in Poland. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
